 Mass. officials report jump in voter turnout during midterms 
 By Colleen Hill and Mark Gardyna Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 4:17 PM EST | Updated : 46 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SPRINGFIELD, Mass. (WGGB/WSHM) - Springfield voters turned out in greater numbers this November. Secretary of the Commonwealth William Galvin announced on Friday that Springfield saw a 25 percent jump in voter turnout. Western Mass News takes a look at what may have brought more people to the polls.
 From the governor’s race to ballot measures, voters in Springfield had plenty to weigh in on this November. City Election Commissioner Gladys Oyola Lopez said the spike in turnout may have been from the ballot questions themselves, “the spike that we’ve seen here locally in increase in voter turnout was really the ballot questions that drove some of the turnout, including the governor’s race as well,” Oyola Lopez said, “the cannabis question was something that it seemed to particularly drive voters to the polls. 
 Massachusetts ballot question 8 sought to eliminate recreational marijuana sales. Statewide, about three-quarters of voters rejected it. But Secretary of the Commonwealth William Galvin said there’s more to the numbers than how many people cast a ballot. Galvin noted automatic voter registration has brought the state to a record number of registered voters. That can make turnout look lower as a percentage — even when the number of people voting holds steady. 
 Voters also had options when it came to how they cast their ballots. Statewide, Galvin said about 13 percent of voters cast their ballots early in person, and nearly a third voted by mail. More than half voted in person on election day. 
 “I think people, since the pandemic, have gotten used to voting in person during early voting and definitely using the vote-by-mail option. They’ve seen that it’s safe, secure, and it’s something that they can do with ease,” Oyola Lopez said.
 In Springfield alone, Oyola Lopez said more than 10,000 ballots were cast by mail- giving voters another way to make their voices heard.
